articles.title: U.S. military planes leave 2nd U.K. base amid reports of Iranian threat
articles.summary: US military aircraft were pictured at Prestwick Airport near Glasgow on Tuesday morning. [BBC] At least 10 US Air Force refuelling aircraft left a second airbase in Britain on Monday. Flight tracking data seen by BBC Verify shows the aircraft left RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk and landed at other American bases in Europe and also at Prestwick Airport in Ayrshire. The Wall Street Journal reported that this was in response to a threat from Iran but the BBC has not independently verified that claim. Monday's departures come weeks after the US withdrew its bombers from RAF Fairford airbase over a suspected Iran-linked security incident. Asked about Monday's flights, an MoD spokesperson told the BBC: "We do not routinely comment on the activity of other nations. Aircraft and other assets move regularly ​according to operational ​requirements." Using public tracking site Flightradar24 BBC Verify has been able to see USAF KC-135 tankers leaving Mildenhall throughout Monday. Two aircraft that left initially flew to US bases in Germany and Italy. The first KC-135 then returned to Mildenhall before heading east and landing at Spangdahlem airbase in Germany. The other aircraft - having flown circuits over Aviano airbase in Italy - flew on to and landed at Spangdahlem. Flight-tracking data also shows eight other US KC-135s left Mildenhall later on Monday. An aircraft that landed at Prestwick in Scotland on Monday is with the Nebraska Air National Guard, meaning it may have been on a regular stop before heading back to its American base. [BBC] About 3,000 military personnel are stationed at RAF Mildenhall, which is around 80 miles (130km) north of London. The BBC has found there is currently very little aircraft movement at the base, and there appears to be no additional security in place around it. The spaces from which the public can photograph aircraft remain open. The base is mostly used for refuelling and maintenance operations - flights carrying US presidents, including Donald Trump, have often used it. It has also been used as a staging area for aircraft and material bound for the Middle East. Air refuelling tankers were "forward deployed" to the region during operations against Iran. Asked about the US evacuating aircraft from RAF Mildenhall, Education Secretary Lucy Powell told BBC Breakfast she could not comment on ongoing operational matters. She added that "we take the security and safety of our bases incredibly seriously" and "we will always act on security intelligence when we need to". A US Air Force spokesperson said its aircraft "rotate between installations and operating locations for a variety of reasons including training and real world requirements". "US military aircraft are hosted in accordance with access, basing, and overflight agreements with our allies and partners. Due to operations security, we will not provide further information on movement of assets," the spokesperson added. Former UK National Security Adviser Lord Ricketts told BBC Radio 4's Today programme: "We are talking about an airbase which houses these large tanker aircraft. Of course, they are large targets, an airbase has a long perimeter, so they are inevitably vulnerable." He added: "Nobody knows at this stage what this information was. I suspect part of it is an abundance of caution." Aircraft left RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk and landed at other American bases in Europe and also at Prestwick Airport in Ayrshire [Reuters] Speaking before reports emerged of the flights leaving RAF Mildenhall, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio was asked on Monday about Iranian threats against American diplomats overseas. "We've addressed it by moving people away from the threat," he said, adding: "Obviously, we're always worried about the safety and security of our personnel and their families overseas. And so, when we see anything that could pose a potential threat beyond a certain threshold, we're going to address it." Monday's departures from Mildenhall follow a security incident at RAF Fairford, a US-operated airbase in Gloucestershire. A major incident was declared after three suspicious vans were seen near that base in September. It later emerged that the US had pulled its bombers out of the base and returned them to America. Two British nationals appeared in court in October in connection with an alleged Iran-linked plot. Eight men have been arrested as part of the counter-terror police investigation. articles.title: Trump backs Hegseth and slams Massie for introducing articles of impeachment
articles.summary: Rep. Thomas Massie, a Republican from Kentucky, reintroduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday, alleging that the embattled Pentagon chief had committed "high crimes and misdemeanors" and abused the power of his office by violating the War Powers Resolution, conducting military operations without congressional authorization and ordering unlawful military actions in several countries. The expected impeachment filing came as Congress returned to Washington, D.C. , to begin a lame-duck session following the historic rout that the GOP suffered in last week's midterm elections . Hegseth is facing intense political backlash over the United States' costly and unpopular war with Iran, which some top Republicans — including  Trump — blame in part for the drubbing that cost them control of Congress. Hegseth said on Monday that he's "not worried about" the impeachment efforts. The defense secretary said he would address the topic at a press conference on Tuesday morning. It would be Hegseth’s first news conference from the Pentagon in six months. "Despite the absence of a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by an attack upon the United States," Massie said in a speech on the House floor, "Secretary Hegseth knowingly executed and implemented unlawful orders to initiate war against a foreign nation." Massie said Hegseth "has demonstrated that he will remain a threat to the Constitution if allowed to remain in office, and has acted in a manner grossly incompatible with his duties and the rule of law." His actions thus "warrant impeachment and trial, removal from office and disqualification to hold and enjoy any office of honor, trust or profit under the United States," the Kentucky Republican said. President Trump has pledged to support Hegseth while he faces impeachment. In a Truth Social post Monday night, Trump defended Hegseth as “the most popular and successful military official” in the country, adding, “Pete Hegseth should be praised, not Impeached. Congress, stand up for Pete!!!” Earlier, Trump told CNN at a White House press conference he would “stand by him,” saying that he believes Massie "has a lot of hatred in his heart." Hegseth leaves a meeting of defense ministers in the Philippines on Oct. 28. Pool via Getty Images Massie — who in May lost his bid for reelection to Ed Gallrein, a Trump-backed challenger, in the GOP primary — first introduced articles of impeachment against Hegseth in September. But House Speaker Mike Johnson later canceled the final scheduled voting day before the midterm recess, delaying a vote. It's unclear whether an impeachment effort will succeed in the House, which is still under Republican control, but Massie told ABC News that he's "confident there will be enough GOP defectors for it to pass." To do so, the resolution requires a simple majority, meaning that just three Republicans would need to vote with all Democrats to prevail. A vote could come as soon as this week. Trump has repeatedly insisted that he is not considering replacing his Pentagon chief, at least not yet. "No, I think he's doing a very good job," Trump told reporters last week. The president also said he was unaware of a report that Hegseth has been quietly angling to fill the U.S. Senate seat that will be vacated by Tennessee GOP Sen. Marsha Blackburn, who was elected as the state's next governor. "I think he's doing a very good job, and I actually think he'd be very popular if he did that. But I haven't heard that at all," Trump said when asked if he would want the defense secretary to fill Blackburn's seat. CBS News , however, reported last week that Trump "has been asking advisers" whether he should stay or go. Hegseth, a former Fox News host who has served as defense secretary since January 2025, has been Trump's most visible cheerleader for the Iran war, which the U.S. and Israel initiated in February and which has led to surging oil prices. He has also been among the advisers urging Trump to restart the war. He and Adm. Brad Cooper, the head of U.S. Central Command, have supported a return to major combat operations against Iran during recent briefings on military options, the Wall Street Journal reported on Nov. 6, while Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff have pushed for diplomacy to end the conflict. The U.S. Capitol building is seen in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 4. Kevin Carter/Getty Images Trump acknowledged on Nov. 4 that the Iran war had partly contributed to the midterm election rout that handed Democrats control of Congress. Vance was unequivocal. "The real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone," Vance wrote in a lengthy post on X . "The reason we lost is the war." The vice president did not call out Hegseth by name. But other Republicans did. Sen. Thom Tillis, a Republican from North Carolina, told CBS News that Hegseth faces "a reckoning." "He is one of the reasons why we don't have the funding or guarantee for defense that we need," Tillis said on election night. "I think after the election, we need to determine whether or not he's the best person to bring those needs to Congress." Tillis, who voted to confirm Hegseth last year, recently called on Trump to fire him. "I have never witnessed more inept management of the brave men and women who serve our country," Tillis wrote in a scathing assessment of Hegseth on X in September. "He is intimidated by competence and retreats to ginning up culture wars instead of soberly attending to the vital work of our national defense and the health and well-being of our fighting force. I urge the President to find a new leader at the Pentagon who will retain and empower our military talent rather than diminish it." Rep. James Comer of Kentucky, the Republican chairman of the House Oversight Committee, said on Nov. 6 that "there's a lot of questions about Hegseth." "We have no idea what the strategy is moving forward in Iran," Comer told NewsNation . "No one's happy about Iran." A fire burns at an oil depot in Tehran, Iran, on March 8 after U.S. and Israeli attacks. Hassan Ghaedi/Anadolu via Getty Images When Democrats take control of both the House and Senate next year, they will have the ability to call for hearings and launch investigations into virtually any aspect of the Trump administration — and Hegseth's handling of the military is high on their list. "In the majority, one of the first things we're gonna do is run Pete Hegseth out of town," Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York, the minority leader who is poised to become House speaker in January, said at a rally last month . Hegseth, for his part, has remained defiant. In a 5-and-a-half-minute video posted to X on Nov. 5, Hegseth defended the Iran war, touted changes he's implemented as Pentagon chief ("We ended the weird and the woke") and praised Trump's leadership while dismissing Massie's impeachment pursuit. "A disgruntled, defeated congressman along with all his Democrat allies has dropped sham impeachment articles against yours truly," Hegseth said. "It didn't work with President Trump and it won't work with me." articles.title: Gas prices drop below $4 a gallon after months of pain at the pump
articles.summary: (Bloomberg) -- US gasoline dropped below $4 a gallon for the first time since July, offering consumers some relief at the pump, although prices remain significantly elevated on a seasonal basis. Most Read from Bloomberg Nvidia Scandal Creates Risk for Entire AI Industry, Not Just CEO Georgia State Race Reversed After Votes Surface on Memory Card Alice Huang, Suspected China Spy, Spent Years in Nvidia’s Orbit MAGA Hardliner Boebert Defeated in Colorado Race, CNN Projects Several Senate Republicans Call for Delaying Leadership Election The nationwide average retail price for regular gasoline slipped to $3.98 a gallon on Monday, according to the American Automobile Association, extending a decline that started in late September. It is the first time the average has fallen below the key psychological level since mid-July. US pump prices surged after the US and Israel launched military strikes on Iran in late February, triggering an energy shock as exports of crude and refined products were disrupted through the crucial Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump last week said it was “largely true” that Republicans lost the midterm elections because of the war in the Middle East. Other supply disruptions have added to the pressure. Escalating Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries, along with lower exports from China, have contributed to a tighter global fuel market. US gasoline prices typically fall heading into winter as driving demand declines, but prices remain about 19% above the seasonal average. There are some signs of relief. US gasoline stockpiles, which have been below seasonal levels since late April, have started to recover, while crude prices have tumbled on hopes for a faster resolution to the war. Gasoline futures have also slumped this month. Still, pump prices typically fall more slowly than they rise, and any renewed conflict between the US and Iran could send gasoline soaring again. The retail price of diesel remains above $6 a gallon after crossing that threshold for the first time in September. articles.title: Several midterm races still haven't been called. Where things stand right now.
articles.summary: The dust has almost settled on the Democratic Party's 2026 midterm landslide — almost . It's clear that Democrats won sweeping victories in the U.S. House, Senate and statehouses nationwide . But some key races remain too close to call, including Senate brawls in deep-red Mississippi and Alaska; Rep. Lauren Boebert's reelection battle in Colorado; and other nail-biter House contests across the South. Here's the latest on how many seats Democrats have won so far — and where things stand in all of the unresolved races. How many Senate seats did Democrats win? Democrats came into the midterms needing a net gain of four seats to win back the Senate. To do that, they had to defend a handful of potentially vulnerable swing-state seats while also flipping at least a few seats in historically red states. That's exactly what happened. Republican efforts to flip blue seats in Michigan, Georgia, Minnesota and New Hampshire all came up well short. Meanwhile, Democrats secured victories to flip seven GOP-held seats in Maine, Texas, South Carolina, Ohio, North Carolina, Iowa and Kansas. Only two incumbent Republican senators in races that drew significant attention were able to win reelection: Florida's Ashley Moody and Nebraska's Pete Ricketts. As it stands, Democrats will enter 2027 with at least 54 seats in the Senate . They have already gained seven seats to give themselves, at minimum, a four-seat majority. Their majority could grow to six if the two remaining undecided races in Alaska and Mississippi go their way. Where things stand in the undecided Senate races Both races are extremely close, with no clear indication of when they might be decided. In Mississippi , Democrat Scott Colom's lead over Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith had grown to 2,536 votes as of Monday evening, according to the Associated Press . Outstanding absentee ballots in the race must be received by Tuesday in order to be counted, according to Mississippi state law. Colom's lead — which stood at just 65 votes on Election Day — has widened gradually in the days since. Even though 97% of the vote is in, AP has yet to call the race because the gap between Colom and Hyde-Smith remains narrow — just 0.27% of all ballots cast. Alaska's ranked choice voting system means it could take significantly longer for a winner to be declared. As it stands, Democrat Mary Peltola holds a lead of 637 votes over Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan, with 74% of ballots counted. The state is expected to have counted nearly all ballots by Nov. 13, with the last remaining votes tallied by Nov. 18. The wait for a final result could become extended if neither Peltola nor Sullivan receives more than 50% of the total first-choice votes. That would trigger a count of ranked choice votes to determine the winner. Under Alaska law, the ranked choice tally cannot begin until Nov. 18, which means a winner wouldn't be declared until two full weeks after Election Day. How many House seats did Democrats win? So far, Democrats have won 254 U.S. House seats — far more than the 218 they needed for a majority. That includes 44 red-to-blue flips. Democrats' 13-point victory in the House popular vote (so far) has been the largest in any midterm since 1974. Where things stand in the undecided House races On Monday afternoon, incumbent GOP Rep. Mario Diaz-Balart of western Miami defeated Democratic challenger Nicole Locklin by about 1,700 votes in Florida's 26th Congressional District. Another 20 U.S. House races remain unresolved. Two of them are in Louisiana, which holds open, nonpartisan "jungle primaries" on Election Day, then sends the top two finishers to a Dec. 12 runoff if no one gets a majority of the vote. One Democrat and one Republican will now go head-to-head next month in Louisiana's 5th and 6th Congressional Districts . In California's 4th and 7th Districts , only Democrats are competing. Officials are still counting ballots in all three races. California also has a nonpartisan jungle-primary system where members of the same party can advance to the general election. Of the remaining 15 races, Democrats lead in five. In Colorado's 4th Congressional District — long considered one of the state's safest Republican seats — GOP firebrand Lauren Boebert trails Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired rear admiral in the Navy, by more than 3,000 votes with just 2% of the vote left to count . After a close 2022 reelection fight in her previous district, Boebert switched to the 4th District for her 2024 campaign and won by about 11 percentage points. Colorado counties have until Nov. 13 to count ballots and upload final results. Right now, Laubacher's lead is too big to trigger an automatic recount. Democrats' next-largest lead is in central Florida's 9th Congressional District , where incumbent Democrat Darren Soto — who was targeted by GOP redistricting efforts — leads Republican challenger Dan Green by roughly 1,500 votes with more than 99% of the vote counted. The state of Florida has announced there will not be a recount in the 9th District because Soto's lead falls outside recount requirements. Soto is expected to win. Democrats' other leads are in Tennessee's 4th Congressional District , Minnesota's 1st Congressional District and North Carolina's 5th Congressional District . The margins in these races are in the 100- to 300-vote range. A recount is likely in Minnesota . Republicans lead in the other 10 unresolved races. Two of the closest are in Florida. Republican Ryan Elijah leads Democrat Bale Dalton by about 1,600 votes in Florida's 7th Congressional District — enough to avoid a recount under Sunshine State law. Meanwhile, Miami-Dade County election officials began a machine recount Monday in Florida's 27th Congressional District , where Republican Rep. María Elvira Salazar leads Democratic challenger Eliott Rodriguez by 1,090 votes, or 0.44 percentage points. That's within Florida's automatic half-point threshold. Nearly all of the other uncalled races where Republicans lead feature incumbent GOP lawmakers fending off strong challenges in reliably red areas: North Carolina's 3rd, 7th and 10th Districts ; South Carolina's 2nd District ; California's 23rd District ; Washington's 5th District and Alaska's only congressional district . The Western states are still waiting on big batches of mail ballots; the Eastern states have mostly finished counting. Republicans' only remaining pickup opportunity is Maine's 2nd Congressional District , where a conservative Democrat retired — and where former GOP Gov. Paul LePage now leads Matt Dunlap, the progressive state auditor, by more than 5,000 votes with just 2% left to count. A ranked-choice vote count will continue in the state despite Dunlap conceding to LePage on Nov. 5. How many governorships did Democrats win? Republican governors have outnumbered their Democratic counterparts for the last 15 years straight (and for 26 of the last 30 years overall). That's given Republicans more opportunities to experiment with new policy ideas, approve congressional maps, influence election procedures, fill Senate vacancies and build executive experience. But this year, Democrats have reversed the "governor gap," flipping five governorships in Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Nevada and Georgia to bring their total to 29 — the party's first gubernatorial majority since 2011. Where things stand in the undecided governor's race Kansas is anything but a blue state; since 1940, it has voted Republican in every presidential election but one — Lyndon B. Johnson's 1964 landslide. But the Sunflower State has elected two Democratic women governors in recent years: Kathleen Sebelius (2003-2009) and term-limited incumbent Laura Kelly (2019-2027). State Sen. Cindy Holscher is seeking to become the third. Holscher leads Republican Ty Masterson, the president of the state Senate, by more than 7,500 votes with nearly all of the ballots counted. Holscher declared victory on Nov. 4, saying that "the people of Kansas made their voices heard, and I'm deeply honored by the trust Kansans placed in me to serve as your next governor." But the race won't be officially over until all 105 Kansas counties complete a legally mandated close-race audit. Masterson said last week that he wouldn't concede before the audit was done. A source close to the Republican senator told the Kansas City Star that Masterson "did not plan to pursue an additional recount and would accept the results if Holscher's narrow win was finalized." Counties will certify their results on Nov. 15. In Alaska , three Republicans and a Democrat are running to replace Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy. Democratic candidate Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins is currently leading, with 49.6% of the vote. Republican Bernadette Wilson is in second, with 29.2% of the vote, with fellow GOP candidates Dave Bronson and Treg Taylor further behind. 76% of the vote has been counted. How many state legislatures did Democrats win? Democrats' gains were also seen at the state level. They flipped more than 500 state legislative seats across the country and turned a total of 12 legislative chambers blue. That includes three states where they flipped both chambers: Arizona, New Hampshire and Wisconsin. After Election Day's results, Democrats will control the House, Senate and governorship in Arizona for the first time since 1966. Democrats also secured a "trifecta" in Wisconsin. They'll hold both legislative chambers in New Hampshire, but the governorship in the Granite State will remain in Republican hands. Democrats regained trifectas in Minnesota, Michigan and Pennsylvania by clinching majorities in the lone GOP-led chamber in their states. They flipped a single chamber in Georgia, North Carolina and Texas, ensuring that Democratic governors in those states won't face unified Republican opposition within their state legislatures. Where things stand in the undecided state legislative races As of Monday evening, only three state legislative chambers — the North Carolina Senate and both chambers in Alaska — remained undecided, according to the AP. articles.title: FBI investigating Nvidia CEO's affair with suspected Chinese spy, Trump says
articles.summary: By Steve Holland, Courtney Rozen, Karen Freifeld and David Shepardson WASHINGTON, Nov 9 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI was looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. Trump said he "was amazed" by allegations about Huang, ‌among the president's closest allies in Silicon Valley. Trump said he had spoken to the CEO, who told him that he had no idea that ‌the woman was a spy. "I know the FBI is looking into it," Trump said. "I think that he'll be in good shape," he added. Nvidia shares closed down more than 4% on Monday after the company's board launched ​an internal investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The probe, announced on Sunday, has put a spotlight on 63-year-old Huang's future given Nvidia's status as the world's most valuable chipmaker and the CEO's role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom. Huang told Nvidia's employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the relationship. The leather-jacketed Huang enjoys rock-star status worldwide, particularly in Asia, where he often mingles freely with fans, taking selfies and signing autographs for his devoted followers. He ‌is Nvidia's fifth-largest shareholder with a roughly 3.6% stake, according ⁠to LSEG data, and keeps a tight grip on the company through an unusually flat structure in which dozens of executives report directly to him. But unlike Mark Zuckerberg's Meta Platforms or Elon Musk's SpaceX, Nvidia has no dual-class shares that would give co-founder Huang majority ⁠voting control. The New York Times reported that Trump was briefed on Huang's relationship with the woman and that she was giving information to the Chinese government, and that the president chose not to act on the information. "The so-called Chinese spy narrative is purely a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters in Beijing. Huang's relationship with Trump ​has ​coincided with several favorable policy developments for the company, and the president has lavished Huang with praise, ​awarding him the nation's highest honor for scientific achievement in October. The ‌same day Trump gave Huang the award, the president disclosed buying up to $1.6 million and selling up to $1 million of Nvidia shares during the summer. 'NOT AN ORDINARY CEO' Nvidia said its board has confidence in Huang, thought by many on Wall Street to be the most important person underpinning the AI trade. Analysts acknowledged uncertainty around succession, but most do not expect the investigation to result in the longtime CEO stepping down. "Nvidia is not an ordinary company and Jensen is not an ordinary CEO; he is Nvidia, clearly sets the long-term strategy and direction, and pulls most of the company's strings himself," said Stacy Rasgon, an analyst at Bernstein. Nvidia shareholders were quick to sue Huang and the ‌company in a proposed class action on Monday, accusing them of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang's ​ties with a suspected Chinese spy. Lawmakers and advocates told Reuters that Congress was more likely to pass ​legislation to tighten China's access to AI chips in light of news of ​Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence agent. US House of Representatives Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Monday that Congress needs more answers ‌and called for the House to pass an annual defense bill ​that includes restrictions on chip sales to China. The ​New York Times reported last month that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities investigated and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset. Megaspeed did not respond immediately to a request for comment on Monday, a public holiday in Singapore. Alice Huang did not ​respond to the New York Times last month when it ‌first reported her relationship with Huang, and Reuters could not determine her location to seek comment on Monday. (Additional reporting by Kyu-seok Shim and Heekyong Yang ​in Seoul, Tom Westbrook in Sydney, Roger Tung and Ben Blanchard in Taipei, Danilo Masoni in Milan and Aditya Soni in Bengaluru; Writing by ​Brenda Goh and Sayantani Ghosh; Editing by Ed Davies, Jamie Freed and Arun Koyyur) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/news/south-korea-says-nvidia-issues-022650481.html

articles.title: California voters reject billionaire tax after opponents argued it would harm the economy
articles.summary: A November rally against Proposition 40 at the Iron Workers Apprenticeship Training Center in La Palma. (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times) California voters have rejected the controversial billionaire tax. Proposition 40 sought to impose a one-time 5% tax on California billionaires ’ assets to try to offset federal healthcare funding cuts. Despite the blue wave in the midterm elections, the novel tax on the ultra-wealthy had trailed from the first day of vote counting and was officially rejected on Monday. Roughly 53% of Californians voted against the measure, while 47% supported it, the Associated Press said when it declared that the proposition had failed. Although the billionaire tax was rejected in the vast majority of counties, the late tally showed major pockets of support in Los Angeles and San Francisco — home to the lion’s share of the state’s 200 billionaires. Orange County, however, voted no by a wide margin. Open the interactive version of this graphic The political battle over the ballot measure and two competing proposals divided the state and was among the most expensive in California history.  More than $400 million had been spent on the three intertwined ballot measures, with more than 90% spent opposing the billionaire tax, according to fundraising disclosures filed with the secretary of state’s office. Billionaires, notably Google co-founder Sergey Brin, poured hundreds of millions of dollars into groups that funded ads to kill the billionaire tax. California Gov. Gavin Newsom, the California Teachers Assn. and Planned Parenthood Affiliates of California are among the powerful Democrats and other Democrat-aligned groups that expressed fears that billionaires would flee the state. Some, including Brin and fellow Google co-founder Larry Page, moved out of California because of the proposal. An onslaught of advertisements against the billionaire tax argued it could impact all Californians, not just the ultra-wealthy. Teachers, firefighters and other middle-class Californians became the face of their campaigns, fueling growing opposition ahead of election day. Read more: California’s billionaire tax battle is playing out on Instagram — with paid influencers Opponents of Proposition 40 said Californians made the “right decision,” calling Proposition 40 a “reckless experiment” that would hurt the state’s economy. The group included the California Medical Assn., California Primary Care Assn. and the California School Boards Assn. “Proposition 40 risked California’s economic competitiveness and fiscal stability, as well as the revenue we rely on to fund our top priorities — from education and healthcare to public safety and infrastructure,” the group said. Leaders of the Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West, which sponsored the proposition, vowed to put a billionaire tax proposal on the 2028 ballot if Sacramento leaders don’t find a way to better support the public health sector. Given California’s volatile budget, which is expected to be particularly problematic next year, it appears unlikely that state lawmakers will find a way to backfill an estimated $100 billion of federal healthcare funding cuts. Read more: Billionaire tax continues to trail as many Californians vote to spare the state’s ultra-rich stars Supporters said the proposed tax on more than 200 California billionaires aimed to raise that amount, with 90% funding healthcare, and the remainder going to schools and food assistance. “Billionaire-funded propaganda may have influenced the outcome of this election, but as hospitals reduce services, emergency rooms close and families lose access to care, the truth will become increasingly difficult to hide,” said Suzanne Jimenez, chief of staff for the SEIU-UHW. “Californians will see for themselves what was at stake.” This will not be the end of the debate about taxing the rich. U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Fremont), who both backed Proposition 40, are pushing for the passage of a federal 5% tax on American billionaires. Earlier this year, they introduced the “Make Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share Act.” Despite Democrats winning control of the House and Senate last week, the legislation will probably face constitutional challenges if it passes. "NTSB investigators have recovered the cockpit voice recorder (CVR) of the Learjet 60 that crashed on Nov. 1 near Greenacres, Florida," the NTSB said on X. The CVR was found at the location of the initial impact​, according to the NTSB. The NTSB said the CVR is being evaluated in the board's Vehicle Recorders Laboratory in Washington, D.C. articles.title: Ole Miss students accused of making racist gestures outside Black students' home
articles.summary: Officials at the University of Mississippi are investigating a video showing three white women outside a Black student's apartment Friday evening, with two of them allegedly making racist noises and gestures captured on Ring camera footage. "[T]he incident is being actively investigated by the appropriate university offices," Vice Chancellor Shawnboda Mead said in a statement Monday, in part, adding, "our staff have reached out to the students directly impacted to offer support, listen to their concerns, and connect them with available resources. We will continue to support them as we work through this process." "Every student deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued at the University of Mississippi. Racism and actions that disparage people because of an aspect of their identity have no place in our campus community," the statement also said. The two women in the video, which was posted to TikTok, are seen briefly stepping toward the door camera, beating their chests while grunting and cooing like monkeys. The third woman glanced towards the camera, but she did not appear to make any gestures or monkey noises. The school said in its statement that it was investigating "the incident." The video had been viewed over 12 million times as of early Monday afternoon. Courtesy Jakiyra Metcalf - PHOTO: Ole Miss University is investigating video appearing to show students making monkey sounds and gestures, allegedly targeting Black students with racist tropes. The incident has sparked outrage online, with many comments decrying the video's apparent use of the racist trope of comparing Black people to monkeys. "The university is aware of a video depicting offensive, hurtful, and unacceptable behaviors that conflict with our university values and we condemn them," Ole Miss told ABC News in a statement. "The university has reached out to those targeted by the actions to share information, resources, and support." The school confirmed to ABC News that the women in the video are students at the university. It did not respond to ABC News' question regarding whether disciplinary action was taken against the students in the video. MORE: 'Racist' actions from counterprotesters at University of Mississippi prompt investigation "It's important to note that student conduct cases, records, and any potential disciplinary action are protected by the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)," university representatives told ABC News. Jakiyra Metcalf, one of the Black students who lives in the apartment, told ABC News that they were expected to meet with university officials on Monday. Metcalf posted the video to TikTok over the weekend. "What do we have to say about this ??" she wrote in her post, tagging Ole Miss. Tasha Bolton, whose daughter is of one of the Black students living in the apartment, told ABC News that the women seen in the video live upstairs in the same apartment building. "The video has been shared with university administration, and we want answers. Specifically, what steps will be taken to address this behavior and ensure accountability?" Bolton posted online . "This is absolutely disgusting and unacceptable. College is supposed to be a place where young adults can learn, grow, and feel safe." Stacy Revere/Getty Images - PHOTO: The exterior of Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oct. 19, 2013 in Oxford, Mississippi. A similar incident occurred at the university in 2024 when a white student directed monkey gestures at a Black woman protesting the war in Gaza. That act was also captured on video. "As a public institution, we are committed to supporting the rights of our students, faculty, and employees to express their views in a respectful manner and to assemble peacefully as guaranteed by the First Amendment," Chancellor Glenn F. Boyce said then in an email response to the incident. "However, some individuals at the demonstration acted in ways that conflict with our university's values. Behaviors and comments that demean people because of their race or ethnicity marginalize them and undermine the values that are fundamental to a civil and safe society." The student who made the gestures toward the Black protester was ultimately expelled from his fraternity. ABC News' Rowan Henchy contributed to this report. articles.title: In a nail-biter Senate race, incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith stays out of view in Mississippi
articles.summary: Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom, left, and GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, right. - Rogelio V. Solis/Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc./Getty Images As the Mississippi Senate race still remains too close to call, Democrat Scott Colom and GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith have taken completely different approaches towards the public. Since Election Day, Colom has held at least eight events and capitalized on the national attention of the race to flood the airwaves and make his case for why Democrats should no longer count out a state historically considered a Republican stronghold. Meanwhile, Hyde-Smith has not been seen publicly since she left her election night watch party just outside of Jackson after declaring that she would remain her state’s junior senator. While Colom has appeared at local universities, a Black-owned bookshop, a vinyl record store, a diner, and a senior citizens center and sat for multiple interviews with the media, Hyde-Smith has made her statements solely on X, including posting a Bible verse about hope on Sunday. “Ultimately, at some point, the senator needs to speak out. Where is Cindy Hyde-Smith?” Colom told reporters on Friday at the senior citizens facility in Jackson. “We want to hear from her. She needs to answer questions. What is her path to victory? She doesn’t have one.” Hyde-Smith’s campaign manager Jake Monssen said in a statement to CNN, “Senator Hyde-Smith and our team are working around the clock across Mississippi to protect the integrity of this election and to ensure every legal vote is counted.” As the Senate returned to session on Monday after a six-week recess, Hyde-Smith repeatedly declined to answer questions from reporters in the Capitol hallways about her election. “We’re still counting votes,” she eventually said as reporters trailed her through the building. Hyde-Smith did not answer when asked if she’ll go to court for a recount if she ultimately loses. Asked if she was surprised by the results of the race, the senator said she was surprised by the reporters following her. The divergent strategies speak to a dynamic that played out across the country this election cycle where Republicans in GOP strongholds like Hyde-Smith, who did not work to get ahead of the worsening national political landscape, were caught flatfooted and now find themselves in a once-unthinkable position. Now, Colom leads the incumbent senator by 2,500 votes in a race that could come down to thousands of provisional ballots, which election officials will vet in the coming days. If he wins, he will be Mississippi’s first Democratic senator in nearly four decades and its first Black senator since the Reconstruction era. Hyde-Smith’s campaign refused Colom’s invitations to debate prior to Election Day and did relatively few campaign events even as Colom was frequently on the trail and appearing with top Democrats like Kamala Harris and Bill Clinton. Even some of Hyde-Smith’s supporters have noticed their senator’s absence and how Colom has filled that void. A sign supporting Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith at a gas station in Brandon, Mississippi, on November 8, 2026. - Ellen Schmidt/AP John, an insurance adjuster from Hyde-Smith’s hometown of Brookhaven who declined to disclose his last name, is disappointed the Republican senator did not win in a landslide. Describing his community as the buckle to the Bible Belt, a county where Hyde-Smith outperformed Colom nearly 2:1, it’s hard for him to picture his home state turning blue. But John said he wished Hyde-Smith matched the television ads that he was inundated by from the Colom campaign. “I would like to personally have seen more campaigning from Cindy,” he told CNN. “I would like to have seen more ads for Cindy and put her name out there a little more. And it may be because she’s an incumbent and maybe didn’t feel like the need was there. I’m not sure. I don’t know.” For F.B. Warren, who has served on school boards with Hyde-Smith, Colom’s campaign should be a wakeup call for Republicans about how to not take Mississippi for granted. “It’s kind of like the team that plays a game of football, baseball, basketball, and they never have competition,” Warren told CNN. “So, in Mississippi and across the country, from the Republican Party standpoint, they got pushed. They now got pushed, so they’re going to have to get better. They’re going to have to campaign better. They’re going to have to have better candidates. They’re going to have to work harder, and that’s the big wake-up call.” His wife, Angie Warren, who owns two small stores in Hyde-Smith’s hometown, reflected on how Democrats did more to capitalize on voter enthusiasm this election season. “I do think that the Democratic Party has a better turnout for elections than the Republican Party. I don’t know why that is. I don’t know if they speak closer to the people and they get out and vote more. But for some reason, the Republican Party doesn’t always have the voter turnout that it needs,” she told CNN. While Mississippi has long been Republican territory, Colom and other Democrats have argued that the headwinds against the party in power and the state’s significant Black electorate made the state fertile ground for a flip this cycle. Further, Hyde-Smith, who was first appointed to the Senate in 2018, underperformed Republicans in 2020 as well, winning a full term by 10 points even as Trump won the state by 16. Democratic candidate for Senate Scott Colom speaks to reporters during a campaign event at the Tougaloo Senior Citizens Center in Jackson, Mississippi, on November 6, 2026. - Ellen Schmidt/AP The early lack of national attention to the race gave Colom a long runway to capitalize on Hyde-Smith’s uneven campaign performance. It wasn’t until late October that the Senate Leadership Fund, the leading GOP super PAC focused on Senate races, made an initial reservation of about $160,000 in Mississippi, according to AdImpact data. That reservation was in response to Senate Democrats announcing that they would spend r oughly $1 million on ads for the race. By that time, Colom had started to galvanize the party behind what was once considered a long-shot bid in a state Trump won two years ago by 23 points. Hyde-Smith has posted on social media since Election Day, including a statement on November 6 stating, “we are not backing down. This election is not over” and vowing to “see this through to the very end!” Mississippi GOP Chair Michael Hurst held a press conference last week to tout the 50-plus volunteer attorneys and observers Republicans had sent across the state, with many more are prepared to jump in to help. “Our attorneys and observers will continue to be in different parts of Mississippi – watching as election commissioners review and process these outstanding ballots, ensuring that our elections are followed and that only ballots which have been legally cast are counted,” he said. unknown content item - Even as both sides prepare for a potential legal battle over the results, Democrat Phillip Rollins told CNN that Colom’s nonstop style channeled the frustration that he and others were feeling in the lead up to the election. “People are fed up,” Rollins, who owns the comic book and record shop where Colom recently campaigned, said. “They need to see the change happen during their lifetime and not have to wait.” This story has been updated with additional details. CNN’s Lauren Fox and Manu Raju contributed to this report. articles.title: Air France and American Airlines jets nearly collide after wrong turn in midair over LAX
articles.summary: The FAA is investigating after two passenger jets narrowly avoided a midair collision shortly after taking off from Los Angeles International Airport when one aircraft reportedly made an unauthorized turn into the other’s flight path. The close call occurred Saturday at approximately 12:20 a.m. after the pilots of Air France Flight 28, traveling from Los Angeles to Papeete, Tahiti, turned into the path of an American Airlines aircraft that had departed from a parallel runway, according to the FAA. Flight tracking data indicates the two planes came within 400 feet vertically of each other, but air traffic controllers quickly stepped in to keep them apart. Flight data shows the paths of an Air France jet and American Airlines plan after takeoff from LAX. (Flight radar) “Air France 028 heavy, fly heading of 270 immediately,” a controller can be heard instructing the Air France crew in ATC audio. The controller then warned the American Airlines flight about the approaching Air France jet. “Traffic alert, traffic 12 o’clock, less than a mile, maintain 2,000." The controller is heard repeatedly asking the Air France pilots why they deviated from their assigned route. "Air France 028 Heavy, you were instructed to climb via SID not, uh, turn to a, uh, heading," an air traffic controller told the pilots. A standard instrument departure, or SID, is a published route programmed into the aircraft's computer to stay on course manually or with auto-pilot, designed to guide aircraft safely away from an airport. Seconds later, ATC asked, "Why did you turn to a heading?" The pilots of the Air France flight said they were instructed to follow a particular departure procedure. United jet may be linked to small plane flipping at Southern California airport “We were instructed to fly SUMMR TWO departure,” a pilot is heard responding. “Possible pilot deviation. I have a number for you to call when you’re ready,” the controller then said. Such a request generally means air traffic control wants the pilots to contact authorities and discuss the incident. “Sorry about that. That aircraft just turned in front of you,” the controller said to the American Airlines pilots after the danger passed. The two aircraft, which likely carried a combined 500 passengers, continued to their destinations without any reported injuries. The FAA is investigating the possible pilot deviation to determine whether the crew failed to follow instructions and whether further action is warranted. With more than four decades as a flight instructor, commercial airline pilot and international pilot for the U.S. Air Force, Captain Richard Levy said this is a first he's heard of this happening. "I worked 41 years for a major airline," he told KTLA's Hailey Winslow. "I’ve never heard of an aircraft flying the wrong departure. And I’ve been in training most of my career, I’m not sure I’ve ever seen someone mis-program it." Captain Levy continued, “And how does that happen? We call it pilot error, a mistake, they may have programmed the wrong departure in the aircraft’s computer.” Though it’s not part of the audio recording of this incident, Levy said a warning inside the aircrafts likely went off. The flight deck is equipped with a “traffic collision avoidance system” that alerts pilots when another aircraft is too close with a “resolution advisory” to “climb or descend," he said. The FAA issued a statement about the incident, saying, "The crew of Air France Flight 28 made an unauthorized turn after departing Los Angeles International Airport and went into the path of another aircraft that departed from a parallel runway. Air traffic control immediately issued corrective instructions to the Air France flight." An Air France spokesperson told KTLA, "Air France confirms that the crew of flight AF028, from Los Angeles to Papeete on 7 November 2026, received a request from air traffic control shortly after take-off to adjust its flight path. The crew immediately followed the instructions before continuing the flight. The aircraft landed normally in Papeete at 5:59 am (local time)." Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. All rights reserved. articles.title: 私募巨头KKR利润爆金币 市场却吓得直往后躲
articles.summary: KKR刚刚交出了一份漂亮得不能再漂亮的成绩单。 11月9日，这家美国私募巨头公布三季报：利润16.5亿美元，同比涨了29%，每股1.78美元，远超华尔街预期的1.59美元。管理费、经营收益、净利润，三项核心指标全部创下历史纪录。 KKR是杠杆收购的祖师爷——1976年创立，靠“借钱买公司、做好了再卖”起家。五十年过去，它早已不只干这一件事，如今管着8040亿美元的资产，横跨私募、信贷、基建、保险，两位联席CEO放话说2030年要干到一万亿。 按账面数字看，一切都在朝一万亿走。但市场根本不信。KKR的股价今年跌了24%，年初最高145美元，现在不到100美元。利润史上最高，股价反而跌了四分之一。 这不是矛盾。这是市场在说：你过去三个月赚了多少我看见了，但你未来三年还能不能赚这么多，我很怀疑。 而市场对KKR未来盈利能力的怀疑，在很大程度上暴露了目前市场所面临的几个最大风险。

articles.title: 当美国无法建设数据中心，会对 AI 产生怎样的冲击
articles.summary: 2026 年 11 月 4 日，美国中期选举结果落定后的第二天上午，OpenAI 的高管们坐到了一起。 据外媒援引知情人士的消息，他们讨论的是要不要重设 2027 年的数据中心容量预期。讨论还没有形成决定，但焦虑已经摆上了台面。 过去几个月，美国各地的大型数据中心项目接连被按下暂停键。得州前任州长 Abbott 从 8 月起冻结了数据中心的并网和空气许可，要求审计到年底；新当选的州长 Gina Hinojosa 承诺，在州议会立法保护居民之前，暂停所有新数据中心审批，而议会会期要到 2027 年 5 月才结束。 俄亥俄新州长 Amy Acton 提出有条件暂停，要求新项目承担全部电力成本、只能建在旧工业用地上；佐治亚新州长 Keisha Lance Bottoms 则准备上任后直接签行政令，暂停全州新建。 据 Tokenpost 统计，今年 7 月到 11 月 4 日，美国至少有 21 个大型数据中心项目被取消，已经接近 2025 年全年的 23 个。Anthropic 在 10 月 26 日提交的招股书里，也把暂停令写进了风险因素：一些辖区正在考虑或已经批准暂停令，可能推迟或阻止它依赖的算力设施，而且反对数据中心的声音正在跨辖区变得更有组织。 如果我们把这股趋势推到极端，去设想这样一个场景，如果美国所有规划中的数据中心都建不成，对当下和未来的 AI，意味着什么？ 01 潜在算力增长被砍掉 50% 为了把推演的边界划清楚，我们设定这样一个极端场景，它建立在三条假设上： 1，全美所有尚未开工的规划项目全部冻结，相当于把目前约 41% 的暂停范围推向全国； 2，已经在建的项目全部按期完工，这和德州等地暂停令只针对新审批的做法一致； 3，芯片照常供应，唯一的硬约束是电和地。我们只推演美国本土，暂不讨论算力外迁。 这个场景下，被卡住的算力规模有多大？据 Newmark 估计，美国数据中心当前用电约 60GW，这里包含所有数据中心，并非全是 AI。在建容量各家口径不同：Cleanview 约 57GW，Wood Mackenzie 约 80GW，DCMap 8 月的统计约 90GW。这部分项目在情景里会照常完工，构成未来几年美国算力的全部增量。 真正庞大的是「规划中、未开工」的部分，DCMap 8 月统计为 228GW，Wood Mackenzie 披露的累计管线超过 430GW，取一个约 230 到 340GW 的区间比较稳妥。 据此粗略推算，在极端情景下，美国数据中心总容量会在 2028 年前后停在约 120 到 150GW，大约是今天的 2 到 2.5 倍，此后不再增长。作为参照，Synergy 此前的预测是美国容量到 2029 年翻倍；而如果管线里的规划全部落地，这个数字本该是今天的 5 倍以上。极端场景砍掉的，是翻倍之后的那一大段增长。 换算成芯片会更直观。1GW 电力大约能带动数十万块 Blackwell 级 GPU：按单卡全口径功耗 1.8 到 2.3kW 理论计算，约 43 万到 55 万块；Abilene 这样的实际园区，约每 GW 27 万块。两三百 GW 的规划被冻结，相当于数千万块最先进的 AI 芯片失去了机房。 亚马逊为 Anthropic 建设的 Project Rainier 园区内部｜图片来源：Amazon 这个情景很极端，但不荒谬。据 Cleanview 测算，新州长承诺暂停的州里，规划容量合计 158.6GW，约占全国的 41%，其中德州 88.4GW、俄亥俄 21.9GW、佐治亚 20.2GW、新墨西哥 11GW、纽约 9.9GW。也就是说，情景 A 里接近一半的冻结，在现实中已经有了对应的政策承诺。2024 年以来被取消的 69 个大型项目里，有 33 个主要因为当地反对。参议员桑德斯还提出了全国性暂停法案，虽然通过的可能性很小。 有一点需要诚实说明，目前规划的数字水分很大。德州电网 ERCOT 的大负荷排队约 474GW、约 1800 个项目，相当于该电网峰值负荷的五倍左右，大部分是占位性质的投机申报。所以极端场景实际砍掉的有效算力，会小于账面数字。即便打掉水分，它依然是一次算力供给的急刹车。 这样一脚「算力刹车」踩下去后，会对 AI 产生怎样的影响？ 02 当下照常，下一代 AI 受阻 如果极端情景明天发生，用户在一两年里其实感觉不到异样。2027 年之前的前沿模型，照常训练、照常迭代。 因为支撑这一代模型的训练基地，都已经建成或接近完工。据 Epoch AI 的数据库，目前已知最大的 AI 园区是 Anthropic 与亚马逊在印第安纳州的 New Carlisle，容量 1037MW；其次是 xAI 的 Colossus 2，946MW。OpenAI 在德州 Abilene 的园区规划 1.2GW，8 栋楼里的 6 栋截至 9 月已经交付，预计年底完工。 OpenAI 位于德州 Abilene 的 Stargate 园区卫星图｜图片来源：Epoch AI 被卡住的，是计划在 2028 到 2030 年登场、需要数个 GW 才能喂饱的下一代模型。 Epoch AI 的数据显示，前沿训练的电力需求每年增长 2.2 到 2.9 倍，目前的前沿训练已经超过 100MW。Epoch 预计，未来一年会有多个园区突破 1GW，大约两年后，最大规模的训练可能用到约 250 万块 H100 等效算力；照这个趋势，到 2030 年，最大单次训练需要 4 到 16GW。 作为对比，今天最大的园区刚刚超过 1GW。Epoch 也指出，数据中心的容量，实际上就是训练规模的上限：园区建多大，模型最多就能训多大。 而那些瞄准 2028 年之后的超级工程，已经有不少撞了墙。 OpenAI 的 Stargate 计划到 2029 年超过 9GW，美国 7 个站点中的多数原定 2027 到 2028 年大规模上线，主要集中在得州、新墨西哥和俄亥俄这几个暂停州。 其中，Abilene 旁原计划的扩建已被放弃；新墨西哥州 Doña Ana 规划 2.45GW 的 Project Jupiter，今年 3 月被州土地办公室否决了供气管道；俄亥俄州 Lordstown 站点，直到 4 月的卫星图像里还看不到大规模施工。 Meta 约 1GW 的 Prometheus 园区也在俄亥俄，只有路易斯安那州目标 5GW 的 Hyperion 避开了这一轮暂停。 新墨西哥州 Doña Ana 的 Project Jupiter 工地卫星图｜图片来源：Epoch AI 这就带出了接下来的疑问，下一代训练的算力基地搁浅之后，AI 的进步会慢多少？ 03 降速，但不会停摆 要回答这个问题，需要把算力增长拆开来看。 据 Epoch AI 统计，2020 年以来，前沿语言模型的训练算力每年增长约 4 到 5 倍。同期训练用电每年增长 2.2 到 2.9 倍。两者之间约 2 倍的差值，主要来自芯片能效的提升，也就是每瓦电能提供的算力在变多。 硬件之外，算法也在帮忙。常用的口径是算法效率每年提升约 3 倍（Ho 等人 2024 年的研究给出约 2.7 倍）。Epoch 后来把后训练也算进去，估计约每年 10 倍，但区间从 2 倍到 50 倍不等，这里采用更稳妥的 3 倍。 现在可以做一个粗略的推算。 正常情况下，AI 每年获得的「有效算力」增长，等于物理算力增长（4 到 5 倍）乘以算法提升（约 3 倍），大约每年 12 到 15 倍。 在情景 A 下，2028 年之后新增电力归零，物理算力增长里最大的一根支柱被抽走，只剩芯片换代带来的能效提升，每年约 2 倍。再乘上算法的 3 倍，「有效算力」的年增速会从 12 到 15 倍，降到约 6 倍。 有效算力年增速拆解：正常情况与极端情景 A 对比（推算）｜图片来源：极客公园 如果换用 Epoch 更乐观的算法口径（每年约 10 倍），正常情况下的有效算力增速是每年 40 到 50 倍，情景 A 下约 20 倍。两种口径下，电力冻结都会让有效算力增速掉到原来的四成到一半左右。算法进步再快，也补不上电力扩张留下的那一块。 两种算法口径下，电力冻结前后的有效算力年增速（推算）｜图片来源：极客公园 这里还有一个隐患。芯片能效的红利，前提是新芯片能顺利装进机房。机房总电量锁死后，供电和散热改造的难度，可能让这 2 倍也打折扣。 即便如此，每年约 6 倍依然是可观的数字。推演下来，结论很清楚： 极端场景下，AI会明显减速，但不会停摆。 不过这笔账只算了训练需要的算力部分，把视野放到整个 AI 的运转上，电量锁死之后，还有一场争夺会立刻开始。 04 Token 限额时代来了 过去算力不够，就去圈地建新机房。在极端场景下，盘子里的电就这么多，分给训练的每一度电，都要从推理、智能体和后训练那里挤出来。 全市场的算力早已向推理倾斜。据德勤预测，推理占全部 AI 算力的比例，2023 年约三分之一，2025 年约一半，2026 年预计达到约三分之二。 推理与训练在全部 AI 算力中的占比变化｜图片来源：极客公园 AI实验室内部也在变。SemiAnalysis 基于 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 合计算力的估算显示，2024 年初，预训练占 67%，后训练和强化学习只占约 5%，推理约 29%；此后预训练占比逐季下滑，二季度 63%，三季度 57%，2025 年降到五成多，后训练占比持续上升，最新估计两者已经相当。有研究者提醒，这是占比变化，实验室总算力翻了很多倍，预训练的绝对量未必减少。 更大的压力，来自产品形态。推理模型在回答前会生成很长的思维链，用户看不到，但每一步都在耗电。Gartner 的数据显示，智能体完成一项任务消耗的 token，是普通聊天的 5 到 30 倍。 高盛预测，2026 到 2030 年，全球 token 总消耗将增长 24 倍。 智能体与 token 消耗的增长｜图片来源：极客公园 把这些数字放进极端情况下固定的电量里，每家实验室都会面对同一道选择题：每一兆瓦，要么拿去训练下一代更大的模型，要么拿去服务现有的用户和智能体。 想调几十万块卡训一个更大的基座模型，就得限制现有用户的调用量；优先保推理、保用户，下一代模型的进度就会落后。 增加电力这条路被堵住以后，剩下的问题，就是在固定的电量和算力下，继续发展 AI，还有什么路可走。 05 四条「补充路线」 在极端场景的压力下，那些过去因为「反正能加卡」而不受重视的省电技术，会变成主流方案： 把硬件的考核指标换成「每瓦电能产出多少 token」。 在电量固定的机房里，把旧芯片换成能效更高的新芯片，是唯一的扩容手段。 英伟达现在首选的指标，就是「每个全口径电力兆瓦每秒输出的 token」，分母里算上的是园区的全部用电，包括散热和网络。这个指标的流行本身就说明，芯片厂商已经默认客户的瓶颈在电，卡的数量反而是次要的。 按英伟达的说法，Vera Rubin 的每瓦性能是 Blackwell 的 10 倍，智能体场景下对比 GB300 最高可达 30 倍。独立测试也给出了接近的结果：CoreWeave 实测，在同一 DeepSeek R1 负荷、相同交互速度下，Vera Rubin NVL72 每兆瓦的 token 产出是 GB200 NVL72 的 10 倍。不过 Rubin 下半年才开始量产，多数客户要到 2027 年才能普遍用上。 英伟达 Vera Rubin NVL72 机柜｜图片来源：NVIDIA 跨机房分布式训练。 暂停令普遍针对的是动辄数百兆瓦的大型数据中心。一个自然的绕行思路，是把训练任务拆散，分到不同地区的中小机房里。政策压力会直接变成对分布式训练的技术需求。 这个方法，巨头们已经在尝试。谷歌说明过，Gemini 是在多个地点的集群上同步训练的；微软把威斯康星和佐治亚的机房连了起来；CoreWeave 与谷歌云宣布了跨云训练。谷歌的 DiLoCo 研究表明，训练可以在普通网络连接的远程设施之间进行，还能容忍硬件故障。 但这个方法的难度不小。DiLoCo 的作者也承认，这项技术目前只能补充超大集群，无法形成替代。2026 年的一项仿真研究发现，机房相距几十到几百公里时，网络延迟会明显削弱计算与通信的重叠，大量算力在等待数据中空转。 研发重心从预训练，转向后训练和强化学习。 预训练对单一超大集群的依赖最高，在极端下最先受限。数个 GW 的集群建不起来，工程师会把精力转向对集群规模要求没那么苛刻的后训练、强化学习，以及混合专家模型、低精度计算等架构改进。Cursor 就公开说过，其 Composer 1.5 模型在后训练上投入的算力，已经超过了预训练。 端侧和小模型给云端分流。 到 2026 年，蒸馏已经是做小模型的主流方法。量化后的小模型能直接在手机 NPU 上处理结构化任务，10 亿参数以下的模型大约每秒能跑 12 到 15 个 token。越来越多应用采用混合模式：本地小模型先处理大部分请求，少数复杂请求再交给云端大模型。 06 约束之下的机会 极端场景卡住的是美国本土的电。对另外两类玩家来说，这道约束反而打开了窗口：已经在效率路线上积累多年的模型公司，以及准备入场的 AI 创业者。 先看前沿和追赶者之间的距离。据 Epoch AI 今年 5 月的测算，最强的开源模型平均落后闭源前沿约 4 个月，大约相当于 GPT-5 和 GPT-5.5 之间的水平差。过去，前沿实验室靠每年十几倍的有效算力增长不断拉开代差；在极端情景下，这个速度降到约 6 倍，新的代差更难建立，追赶者需要追的距离会变短。 再看效率路线上的先行者。DeepSeek、Qwen、Kimi、GLM、MiniMax 等中国模型公司，一直以开源、低成本和混合专家架构见长，这条路线已经反映在使用数据上。 据 OpenRouter 与 a16z 的联合研究，中国开源模型在该平台的 token 占比，从 2024 年底的约 1.2% 涨到 2025 年的近 30%；进入 2026 年，多家统计给出的比例在五到六成之间。 a16z 合伙人 Martin Casado 还估计，使用开源技术栈的创业公司里，约八成在跑中国模型。OpenRouter 只是一个平台，不包含 ChatGPT 自家流量和企业私有部署，但趋势很清晰： 当整个行业都要回答「每度电能产出多少智能」这个难题，长期在这道题上下功夫的团队，手里的经验会更值钱。 来源： 极客公园 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 公募又“卷”新赛道了，继Agent之后，下一个ETF Skill时代来临
articles.summary: 公募基金的AI应用进入第三阶段。 日前，在AI工作平台WorkBuddy上，悄然出现了一个名为“华泰柏瑞ETF_SKILL”。这个Skill(技能，类似AI平台上的程序)能够完成查询ETF资料、费率、基金经理标签、收益率等一系列工作，弥补了相关AI平台上，官方数据缺乏的不足。 事实上，业内推出Skill的公募机构此前已有几家包括华宝基金、易方达基金、南方基金等，据说业内头部机构华夏基金、嘉实基金、广发基金等可能也在筹划相关的Skill。 一场新的AI竞争正在展开。 ETF Skill能干啥？ 笔者试用了华泰柏瑞和易方达的Skill，发现他们确实能够为ETF投资者或潜在投资者提供一些关键信息。 发布机构将净值、规模等ETF底层数据，打包成可被AI智能体直接调用的“技能”。用户在自己的AI助手中安装后，只需用自然语言提问，即可马上获取相关信息。 比如，通过自然问句询问该Skill相关问题，相关Skill会给出一个比较直接、周到的回答（下图）。 考虑到目前AI平台上，权威、可靠的金融底层数据比较缺乏，相关公募提供自己发布的Skill，有助于缓解平台上数据缺乏的问题。 先入场者图谱 目前已有四家基金公司正式上线ETF Skill，都是业内ETF的领跑机构，也是相关AI应用比较积极的公募基金公司。 易方达依托“指数直通车”搭建，支持个股反向检索重仓ETF。 南方基金在“首趋E指”上线，折溢价跟踪受到关注。 华宝基金推出“ETF小龙虾”标准化技能。 华泰柏瑞上线ETF_SKILL，贯通全流程数据需求。 除已上线的四家之外，华夏基金、嘉实基金、广发基金等也正在筹备或即将进入这一领域，头部指数机构正逐步在AI入口处集体布局。 差异化新赛道选择 上述机构积极布局Skill的原因，可能是想在新的平台上，提供差异化服务。 可以想象，当越来越多的人习惯在AI对话框里问ETF怎么选，那些优先推出类似功能Skill的公司，可能就容易占住先机。 毕竟，哪家基金公司的数据能被AI调用，哪家就在入口占住了位置。 事实上，类似的策略性安排，在业内此前也不乏其例。 华泰柏瑞在推出ETF_SKILL之前，曾举办全国首届ETF AI交易巅峰赛，支持自带Agent调用行情检索、模拟交易等Skills。赛事期间，Skills调用超过60万次，一定程度上验证了Agent调用ETF数据工具的需求热度。 ETF Skill的高频批量数据力 值得注意的是，除了占住新的流量入口外，ETF Skill本身的强大功能也会是吸引人的一个重要因素。 ETF Skill不是简单的查询工具，它的核心竞争力体现在高频批量、跨产品的数据任务场景中。 比如，易方达的“指数直通车”里附加的ETF_Skill里就可以实现更直接的投顾咨询功能。 包括“批量筛选与横向对比”。方便投资者比较某个类型产品——比如中证红利——里的所有ETF，并按特定要求——比如过去5个交易日申赎净流入——实现排序。 此外，“股票反查ETF”等也是比较受ETF短线投机者欢迎的功能。 并非开箱即用 还需要提醒的是，多数基金公司的Skill，并不像华泰柏瑞那样可以直接在WorkBuddy里找到。 而是需要，使用者在查询前，先将相关Skill产品的代码，复制到相应的AI工作平台里。并提前申请用户API Key，才能完成使用。 从复制安装指令、到获取密钥，这一过程过于繁琐，所以，往往并不适合没有相关程序应用基础的普通投资者。 这可能是上述Skill，未来需要改进的地方。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.summary: 预览内容 在这次中期选举之前，不管是国内还是国外，很多卖方研报都提到，如果民主党获胜，会对市场造成一定冲击。但从上周四的市场表现，以及上周五力度非常弱的反弹来看，市场明显没有完全准备好。 我觉得这里面有两个原因。 第一个，虽然大家都觉得民主党会赢，但此前普遍预期的是51个、52个参议院席位，最多看到54个。最后，它的确拿到了54个席位，赢得比很多人原先预期的要多。 第二个，我觉得更关键的是，它赢得非常干脆。在美国不同地区，投给民主党的比例都有上升。有些地方，与其说是民主党赢下了这场选举，不如说是大家不愿意把票投给选票上的共和党候选人。 这就要求市场重新思考未来的很多假设，其中一个很重要的问题，就是数据中心。 这几天，我看到一些自己比较能接受的说法。比如，已经审批通过的数据中心，要马上全部撤回、不准修建，我觉得会存在很多困难，法律上也不一定完全允许…… 点击 此处 或下方图片解锁完整版内容，继续阅读。

articles.title: 日本2nm，悬了！
articles.summary: 日本砸下超过2万亿日元，想重新杀回先进制程市场，但现在看来，这个计划可能没有想象中那么顺利。 据彭博社报道，日本政府支持的晶圆代工企业Rapidus，已经落后于原定的技术开发进度。公司此前承诺在2028年3月前实现2nm芯片量产，但如今这一目标可能难以兑现。 问题出在SRAM。 知情人士透露，Rapidus至今还没有成功制造出能够正常工作的SRAM存储单元。而按照原定计划，公司需要在今年夏季之前完成这一关键技术突破，才能确保后续2nm工艺开发和量产进度。如今这一节点未能实现，意味着Rapidus至少已经落后数月。 这不是一个可以轻易绕过去的问题。对于2nm先进逻辑芯片而言，SRAM是必不可少的组成部分，也是检验制造工艺是否真正成熟的重要环节。 为什么SRAM如此重要？ 现代CPU、GPU以及AI加速器内部，都需要大量SRAM作为缓存，用来存储临时数据和指令，减少处理器访问外部存储器的时间。一颗先进处理器可能集成数亿个SRAM存储单元，这些单元必须在极小的尺寸下稳定工作。 问题是，SRAM对制造工艺的要求非常苛刻。一个存储单元通常由多个晶体管组成，晶体管之间需要保持精确的电气特性和匹配关系。进入2nm时代，器件尺寸进一步缩小，哪怕是非常微小的制造偏差，都可能影响存储单元的读写能力和数据保持稳定性。 所以，制造出可以工作的晶体管，并不意味着已经具备制造完整处理器的能力。SRAM能否正常工作，实际上是先进逻辑工艺必须解决的一道关卡。 这也让Rapidus目前的处境显得有些尴尬。 去年7月，Rapidus曾宣布成功制造出可工作的晶体管，这被视为其2nm研发取得进展的重要一步。但从那以后，公司公开披露的技术进展主要集中在工艺设计套件（PDK）的发布。如今，连SRAM这一关键环节都尚未突破，距离真正实现完整芯片制造和量产，显然还有不少工作要做。 而且，Rapidus面对的问题不只是SRAM。 据知情人士透露，公司目前还在解决洁净室内部的粉尘和颗粒物控制问题。对于先进制程来说，制造环境中的微小颗粒都可能造成缺陷，进而影响芯片良率。工艺开发、设备调试、环境控制和良率提升，任何一个环节出现问题，都可能拖慢整体进度。 Rapidus原定在2027财年下半年启动量产，也就是2028年3月之前。如今，这个时间表正面临越来越大的压力。 日本政府显然不希望这个项目轻易失败。 Rapidus成立于2022年，背后集结了日本多家大型企业，并获得政府大规模资金支持。截至目前，日本政府已经正式安排超过2万亿日元（约130亿美元）的公共资金投入。日本希望借助Rapidus重新建立先进逻辑芯片制造能力，减少对海外先进制程产能的依赖。 但与台积电、三星和Intel相比，Rapidus最大的短板就是缺乏成熟的先进制程量产经验。竞争对手已经在不断推进下一代工艺，Rapidus却还在补齐从晶体管到SRAM、从工艺开发到制造整合的基础能力。 更值得关注的是，Rapidus内部对于量产目标似乎也存在不同理解。 此前，公司独立董事Yoshimitsu Kobayashi曾表示，Rapidus的目标是实现至少80%的量产良率，也就是每生产五颗芯片，至少有四颗能够正常工作。不过，CEO Atsuyoshi Koike和代表董事Atsuo Shimizu并未完全认同这一标准是所有管理层共同采用的定义。 这也从侧面反映出，Rapidus距离真正的商业化量产，还有不少现实问题需要解决。 对于日本政府而言，Rapidus已经不仅仅是一家芯片公司，而是日本半导体产业重新争夺先进制造能力的重要抓手。日本经济产业大臣赤泽亮正上个月也表示，政府准备继续支持Rapidus，直到公司具备独立财务运营能力。 Rapidus方面则回应称，仍在全力推进原定量产计划，并表示技术开发细节属于保密信息。 当然，现在就断言Rapidus的2nm计划失败还为时尚早。即使无法赶上原定时间表，公司未来仍有机会通过延长研发周期实现目标。 但这次SRAM问题暴露出一个现实：先进制程竞争，远不只是建设晶圆厂、采购设备和引进技术那么简单。真正难的是把晶体管、存储单元、工艺整合和良率全部做出来，并且稳定地生产。 日本想重新拿回先进制程的话语权，Rapidus还有一场硬仗要打。 来源： 半导体行业观察 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 第三批互惠便利资金“火线入市”，至少10家券商官宣买入股票
articles.summary: 担当稳定市场重任的第三批证券、基金、保险公司互换便利（简称：SFISF）进入集中落地阶段。 截至11月10日，已有至少10家券商“官宣”已完成第三批互换便利项下的首批股票买入，包括中信证券、国泰海通、中金公司、银河证券、招商证券、中信建投、华泰证券、东方证券、财通证券、浙商证券等。 从公告推出第三批SFISF，再到参加招标，再到获得资金并入场。全程时间不到十天，堪称历史上罕见的“火线入市”。 又有两家大券商公布买入进程 11月9日，中信建投、华泰证券、浙商证券先后披露参与第三批SFISF业务——完成回购融资——并于当日完成首批股票买入操作。 中信建投表示后续将 用足用好互换便利工具，进一步增持股票 ；华泰证券明确将持续 加大对A股股票及股票ETF的配置力 度；浙商证券表示下一步将继续用好互换便利政策工具， 持续开展权益市场的长期资产配置 。 此前，11月6日已有一批机构率先完成买入，包括中信证券、中金公司、国泰海通、银河证券、招商证券、东方证券、财通证券。 业内观察可以发现，此次SFISF资金的使用进程迅速、买入坚决、效果也较为明显。 千亿总盘子已“落地”多少？ 总体上看，目前已经公布确认中标第三批SFISF的26家券商中，至少有12家披露了详细的中标金额，其中规模领先的机构都已表态开始入市。 从规模看，中金公司此次以163亿元的规模领先全行业； 国泰海通与中信证券两家龙头券商，每家各100亿元，可谓中规中矩。 此外，相对融资规模居中或靠前的券商还有国投证券60亿元、东吴证券、招商证券、东方证券各50亿元、浙商证券40亿元，财通证券30亿元。 长城证券、国联民生、华福证券分别融资20亿元、15亿元和12亿元。 另有14家券商确认中标但暂未披露具体金额的机构包括：华泰证券、广发证券、申万宏源、银河证券、国信证券、中信建投、中泰证券、东方财富证券、国金证券、兴业证券、平安证券、红塔证券、光大证券、方正证券。 业内预计，后14家机构的规模应该不会大于已经公告的大多数机构。 公募基金融资金额仍未披露 第三批投标机构从20家扩充至31家，公募的参与家数有所增加，目前已经官宣参与的基金公司包括华夏、易方达、博时、鹏扬等公募机构。但截至目前，仍然没有任何一家公募基金披露具体中标金额。 业内预计，由于公募机构主要是代人理财，自身可投资资产不会太多，因此，大概率是“量力而为”。 同时，业内擅长债券投资的鹏扬基金此次格外积极，或许该机构有自己的策略也未可知。 从表态看，华夏基金表示，SFISF支持机构以债券、股票ETF、沪深300成分股等资产作抵押，有利于进一步盘活资产，统筹安排股市、债市等不同市场间的流动性。 易方达基金表示，将用好互换便利工具，秉持长期投资、价值投资理念，加强产品创新，更好满足不同投资者需求，以更高质量服务居民理财需求与实体经济发展，共同增强资本市场韧性与信心。 鹏扬基金进一步指出SFISF“以券换券”盘活存量资产，不新增基础货币投放，低成本资金定向投向权益投资与做市业务，机构资金面得到有效托底。 而更令人鼓舞的是，由于SFISF的多次使用，未来这项机制或许可以成为专业投资机构“常备”的低成本融资渠道，它对是市场的积极影响还在积淀之中。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: Hitcard还不是“A股卡牌第一股”
articles.summary: 11月10日，停牌一周的亚玛顿（002623.SZ）复牌涨停，股价报21.21元/股，总市值约41亿元。 推动股价上涨的，是一家卡牌公司的跨界收购。 前一日晚间，亚玛顿公告称，卡牌品牌Hitcard背后的上海骑形网络科技有限公司（下称“骑形网络”），拟斥资6.8亿元受让公司20%股份。交易完成后，Hitcard创始人赵云鹏将成为亚玛顿实际控制人。 这让Hitcard距离A股资本市场更近了一步，却还不足以让它成为真正的“卡牌第一股”。 根据协议，骑形网络及其实际控制人承诺，自股份过户完成之日起36个月内，不向上市公司注入自身及关联方持有的资产。 同时，骑形网络承诺受让股份60个月内不转让、36个月内不质押。 对于此次跨界收购，骑形网络向华尔街见闻·信风回应称，看重的是亚玛顿在超薄特种玻璃、物理钢化及纳米镀膜等领域积累的制造能力，将其定位为一笔中长期产业投资。 至于未来的业务协同，骑形网络表示，双方将保持独立运营，目前不存在已确定但未披露的业务协同方案。 卡牌生意逆风期 Hitcard对资本市场的兴趣并非始于此次收购。 Hitcard品牌创立于2021年，运营方为骑形网络。此后，公司陆续获得泡泡玛特、红杉中国种子基金、阅文集团等投资方支持。 2024年，公司收入约4亿元，同比增长超过600%；2025年上半年又完成新一轮融资，同年9月传出推进上市的消息。 不过，卡牌企业的上市窗口并不宽裕。 2025年6月，国内卡牌龙头卡游通过港交所上市聆讯，此后迟迟未能启动发行，招股书于同年10月失效。 2026年初，旗下拥有卡卡沃品牌的Suplay递交港股上市申请，半年后招股书同样失效。 两家公司上市不顺，发生在卡牌消费市场快速降温之际。 弗若斯特沙利文数据显示，2025年中国非对战式卡牌市场GMV由321亿元降至235亿元，同比下降26.8%。其中，单价较低的消费级收藏卡市场缩水超过40%。 进入2026年，市场压力进一步从卡牌蔓延至更广泛的IP潮玩及衍生品领域。 卡牌行业垂直研究机构《卡有江湖》负责人李懒懒告诉信风，今年行业经营情况不佳，渠道库存水位虽然有所下降，但活跃玩家也明显减少。 需求变化已经影响企业的经营策略。 2026年一季度，卡游传统卡牌仅占新品约四分之一，重心向更广泛的“谷子”品类倾斜；集卡社的卡牌新品占比，也从2025年初的42.9%降至今年二季度的15.5%。 行业需求收缩之际，曾经推动Hitcard增长的高频上新模式，或面临成本与盈利能力的双重考验。 2025年12月，赵云鹏在接受华尔街见闻·信风采访时介绍，Hitcard采取多IP、限量、高频上新的模式，每月推出10款以上产品，并建有约2万平方米的自有工厂。 影视IP是Hitcard的一大特色。公司曾围绕《庆余年》《难哄》等热门剧集开发收藏卡，也覆盖《全职高手》《斗破苍穹》等文学、动漫IP。 但上游内容供给正在收缩。据云合数据，2026年上半年国产长剧上新数量同比下降20%。随着长剧市场向精品化、头部化发展，能够持续带动衍生消费的热门IP争夺可能更加激烈。 外部IP授权不仅意味着持续的授权成本和续约风险，消费者对作品、角色的喜爱，也未必能够转化为对卡牌品牌的长期黏性。 与此同时，多IP、小批量、高频上新的生产模式，也让Hitcard难以像头部企业一样充分发挥规模效应。 赵云鹏此前向信风透露，Hitcard平均毛利率约30%，通过让渡部分利润投入产品设计和工艺。今年9月，他又向虎嗅表示，随着规模化生产和材料管理改善，毛利率正向40%提升。 相比之下，卡游2024年收入超过100亿元，集换式卡牌毛利率达到71.3%。 这意味着，Hitcard仍需持续投入资金争取IP、开发新品，并在维持销售规模的同时改善利润空间。 在此背景下，收购亚玛顿又是一笔不小的资本支出。 根据协议，6.8亿元交易对价中，自有资金比例不低于50%，其余部分不排除通过并购贷款筹措。公告同时明确，收购资金不存在直接或间接来源于上市公司及其关联方的情况。 与此同时，骑形网络正在办理注册资本由18.1093万元增至1亿元的手续。 骑形网络向信风回应称，此次增资系“结合自身实体制造资产规模、产能建设及中长期经营发展规划所推进的常规安排”，旨在进一步充实企业自身的资本实力。 不过，公司尚未披露增资的实缴安排，以及至少3.4亿元自有资金的具体来源。 这笔收购能否为Hitcard带来新的资本运作空间，以及骑形网络如何平衡原有业务投入与上市公司经营，仍有待观察。 绕不开的重组上市门槛 Hitcard并非近期唯一尝试通过存量上市公司接近资本市场的卡牌企业。 另一家是“姚记系”旗下的上海真友趣文化科技有限公司（下称“真友趣”)。 真友趣由A股上市公司姚记科技董事长姚朔斌与卡牌行业从业者盛川联合创立，其运营着文化品牌“闪魂”，主要围绕《第五人格》《英雄联盟》等游戏IP开发卡牌。 2025年8月，真友趣宣布完成数亿元首轮融资，由高瓴创投领投，高榕创投、凯辉基金跟投。 几个月后，姚朔斌通过个人全资持有的姚记资本，以1.65亿港元取得港股澳达控股75%股份。 这家原本从事机电工程业务的上市公司，随后开始经营卡牌相关业务，并于今年更名为耀宝控股（Yaopop Holdings）。 2026年上半年，耀宝控股卡牌相关业务实现收入约833万港元，占总营收21.5%。 但是目前尚无明确公开信息表明，“闪魂”运营主体已整体注入上市公司。 两笔交易的共同点在于，卡牌产业相关资本都选择先收购与原有业务关联不大的上市公司控制权，而非直接推动主营业务IPO。 香颂资本董事沈萌对信风分析，目前A股对游戏与衍生品类企业IPO缺少明确的政策支持导向，企业选择其他资本化路径，更多受到IPO政策环境的影响。 至于两家为何分别选择A股和港股，沈萌认为，主要取决于收购方能够接触到哪个市场的资源，以及能够达成怎样的交易条件。 事实上，两地资本市场都对借壳上市设置了严格限制。 根据A股相关监管规则，上市公司控制权变更后的36个月内，如果向收购人及其关联方购买资产，并达到规定的规模或业务变化条件，可能构成重组上市，面临更严格的审核。 港交所同样设有反收购行动规则，防止企业通过分步交易规避新上市要求。 沈萌表示，两地对于控制权变更后的资产注入均有严格要求，但A股在实际审核尺度上更难从公开规则中完全判断。 “在目前的监管环境下，如果希望最终通过资产整合实现业务上市，交易双方需要更精细地设计交易结构，尽可能避免触发重组上市条件。”沈萌说。 此前也存在控制权变更后、36个月内完成关联资产收购的案例。 2020年，天津普林实际控制权变更；2023年5月，公司启动对泰和电路的收购，最终通过现金收购及增资取得其51%股权，交易完成时距离控制权变更尚不足三年。 由于未触发重组上市的认定标准，这笔关联资产交易得以完成。 不过，天津普林与泰和电路均从事印制电路板业务，属于同业资产整合，与骑形网络跨界收购光伏玻璃上市公司的情况存在明显区别。 对于骑形网络而言，即便期限届满，资产注入仍需接受监管审查。如何管理缺乏业务协同性的亚玛顿，以及实现投资回报，依然有待明确。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 联想发布混合词元工厂，2027年将建成1.5万P算力集群
articles.summary: 11月10日，联想集团（ 0992.HK ）在张家口发布万全混合词元工厂品牌，配套的母本工厂落地张家口。发布会上，联想集团与张家口市政府签署合作协议。 按联想披露的计划，2027年，联想将在张家口建成1.5万P的异构算力集群和约100兆瓦的智算中心，年词元产量超过2000万亿个。 联想集团高级副总裁、中国方案服务业务群总经理戴炜介绍，联想企业智能体系由三层混合动力构成，底层是联想问天AI基础设施，顶层是联想擎天、百应智能体解决方案和服务，本次发布的万全混合词元工厂处在中间层。 联想表示，混合词元工厂的作用是把底层算力转化为面向AI应用场景的词元供给。混合词元工厂由两部分组成，一是智算中心的建设、运营和运维，二是xCloud联想智能云。 智能云中的词元中枢（Token Hub）统一纳管私有云和公有云资源，通过模型路由和推理资源池的动态调配输出词元，公司称这一模式把私有化部署的词元和公有词元按场景组合供给。 公司为母本工厂设定了五项指标，包括年词元产量超过2000万亿个、每秒词元输出量提升5倍、词元良品率超过99.9%、百万词元综合成本在现有基础上降低70%、电能利用效率（PUE）低于1.1。 联想还计划与湖南广电在长沙建设面向影视和短剧制作的混合词元工厂，按公司预计，合作项目制作成本降低一半，生产周期缩短60%，月产成片超过1200小时。 戴炜表示，张家口和长沙只是起点，公司将结合各地资源禀赋，落地不同产业特色的混合词元工厂，方向覆盖智能制造、重工业、教育、内容制作、算力出海等。 词元工厂并非新概念。今年4月17日，联想在2026政企合作伙伴大会上正式发布词元（Token）工厂产品，本次发布会是该产品的品牌化升级，叠加母本工厂规划与张家口落地。 行业内，业务范围向词元生产与运营延伸的企业不止联想。 据公司披露，协创数据的TokenShare平台已上线，上半年智能算力产品及服务收入32.16亿元，同比增长163%；利通电子上半年AI算力业务收入12.74亿元，同比增长162%，并披露不超过50亿元的定增预案，其中40亿元用于智算中心建设；弘信电子与趋境科技达成战略合作，旗下无锡、厦门两大AI Token工厂已完成技术适配与试点落地。 张家口市委书记刘文萍在致辞中介绍，张家口是“东数西算”工程京津冀枢纽节点，也是全国唯一国家级可再生能源示范区，已建成数据中心55个，投运机架107万架，智算规模31万P，可再生能源装机年内将突破5000万千瓦，到北京的传输时延不足2毫秒。 今年9月，联想集团与张家口市政府签署战略合作协议，提出共同打造绿电输入、词元输出的算力产业，当天签约的母本工厂项目由张家口市数据和政务服务局局长刘永刚与联想集团副总裁、全球基础架构和智能云总经理姚振宇代表双方签署。 国家信息中心信息化和产业发展部主任单志广援引国家数据局监测数据称，全国日均词元调用量从2024年初的约1000亿次增长到2026年6月的500万亿次。戴炜在演讲中预计，国内词元年消耗量将从2026年的10亿亿个增至2030年的3500亿亿个。 他还提到，在模型聚合平台OpenRouter上，中国模型的调用量占比已从年初的5%升至11月初的55%。 联想集团执行副总裁兼中国区总裁刘军在致辞中称，公司上一财年营业额为5899亿元，上一财政季度营收突破1800亿元，同比增长43%。联想财报显示，该财季营收1834亿元，其中基础设施方案业务（ISG）收入579亿元，同比增长98%，AI服务收入同比增长141%。 上述产能、成本与质量指标均为公司目标值，比较基准未披露。此次发布会上提到的词元良品率，具体测算方法仍有待进一步说明。词元服务的收入口径、母本工厂约100兆瓦智算中心的资本开支归属暂未披露。 圆桌对话环节，中信建投证券（ 601066.SH ）计算机行业首席分析师应瑛提到三项判断标准。 一是企业使用AI的投入产出比能否算清楚，2027年将是重视ROI的起始年。二是AI能力的价值将持续提升，AI产业链没有统一的估值标准。对词元工厂这类算力运营企业，她认为应更看重利润率、折旧、电力成本和现金流。三是规模化交付能力的形成能否显著优化成本。 会后群访中，应瑛对华尔街见闻等媒体表示，词元工厂模式的核心作用是降低企业使用AI算力的综合成本。相比纯公有云，混合部署更贴合国内央国企对数据安全、版权合规的采购要求。 应瑛提到，资本市场把词元工厂这类业务定义为New Cloud（新一代云平台），估值逻辑的核心关注点是盈利质量与现金流，可以参考国内外CSP的盈利能力，例如毛利率超过15%等，是业务质量的参考指标。未来三年，产业链的新增利润边际变化有望逐步从底层算力芯片向词元运营和应用环节转移。 联想预计，张家口母本工厂2027年建成投运，2030年算力集群规模扩大10倍。母本工厂的建设进度、词元服务收入能否在后续财报中单独辨识，以及70%降本基准的补充说明，是观察这一模式兑现情况的下一组节点。 风险提示及免责条款
